subject: 5x vs 10x base coverage in methylkit for downstream analyses

messages.author: d185672db11eeda1
messages.subject: 5x vs 10x base coverage in methylkit for downstream analyses
parts:
Dear Altuna

using filterByCoverage, i wanted to include bases with 5x coverage in my analyses and compare the results with 10x coverage, i expected higher number of differentially methylated Cs when i applied 5x coverage, however the results are exactly similar between both scenarios. im wondering if my codes were correct or maybe i have done something wrong ?


filtered.myobj.10=filterByCoverage(my.methRaw,lo.count = 10, lo.perc = NULL, hi.count = NULL, hi.perc = 99.9)
filtered.myobj.5=filterByCoverage(my.methRaw,lo.count = 5, lo.perc = NULL, hi.count = NULL, hi.perc = 99.9)

thanks in advance

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] 5x vs 10x base coverage in methylkit for downstream analyses
parts:
you need to read methylation calls with at least 5X coverage to be able filter coverage as in the examples you have sent. I think by default we create methylation call files with at least 10X coverage per position. There must be documentation on this, and we discussed this many times on the forum

Best,
Altuna

messages.author: d185672db11eeda1
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] 5x vs 10x base coverage in methylkit for downstream analyses
parts:
yes and thank you for that, so i tried different combinations

A and B) reading methylation call with at least 5X coverage using min.cov argument then filtering the reads using lo.count = 10 and 5 argument
C and D) reading methylation call with at least 10X coverage using min.cov argument then filtering the reads using lo.count = 10 and 5 argument

and here is the results

A) min.cov 5 + lo.count 5 =  545 Cs
B) min.cov 5 + lo.count 10 =  300 Cs
C) min.cov 10 + lo.count 5 = 300 Cs
D) min.cov 10 + lo.count 10 = 300 Cs

as i expected, results for B, C and D are quite similar, No surprise. However, i expected to see all those 300 Cs again in alternative A too, because B is a subset of A. but i extracted only 118 of them. how it possible? 

Best regards
On Monday, June 3, 2019 at 9:47:53 PM UTC+2, Altuna Akalin wrote:
i think that function uses 10X coverage by default, you should be able to change  that via arguments

messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] 5x vs 10x base coverage in methylkit for downstream analyses
parts:
B C and D should be the same and the end result is always 10x filter. You can check if A and B has the same CpGs without the lo.count threshold. If they are from the same BAM/SAM file they should be the same. I can’t think of a reason why they shouldn’t be. 

Best
Altuna
